title: The Old Flame
subtitle: Give the twentieth century a hug, my beautiful, fiery friend!

trails.title: Mural
trails.description: The paint's hues have faded, through clear lines remain engraved on the hard rock. Soon after, they found traces of the spring's mouth.

trails.title: Sports Field Entrance
trails.description: Stepping through the magnificent gate, we now embark on a new journey.

trails.title: Uluru Stadium
trails.description: They run excitedly, like guests drinking capriciously at a banquet, holding up their glasses to celebrate, but ending up hungover.

trails.title: Vertin's Suitcase
trails.description: You must leave the way you came. Familiarize yourself with the world after a thousand years, and understand how to master the flames.

trails.title: Event Program
trails.description: A list of sporting events for the Uluru Games.

content.text: List of Uluru Games Sporting Events (Provisional Version)

Arcanum-Themed Events

[Track and Field] 



The use of arcane skills, such as vaporization, blink, and flying, is permitted.

Potions and special vehicles are strictly prohibited. Requires implementable drug testing procedures to be designed. For example, random sampling before the start of the competition and standardized drug testing procedures for the top six athletes in each event after the competition.



The world record for this event was set by Carlos Castillo, the Cuban flying mouse, in 1924. By the time of his retirement, he was still unable to break his own record.

Mr. Pavia once surpassed this height in training—I witnessed it with my own eyes! I'm really looking forward to seeing him perform out on the field.



There are still uncertainties regarding the distinctions between certain vehicle drivers and the vehicles themselves, such as participants racing in vehicles like UFOs, wooden horses, and artificial satellites.

The individual event rules will provide more detailed information on this situation to avoid any potential complications regarding the referee's decision-making duties.

[Combat Events]



The competition venue needs to be set up next to a medical station.

Guardrails and warning lines need to be placed around the arena to prevent excited spectators from entering the field of competition and disrupting the competition schedule.



Competitors must tame strange water beasts, mount them, and race them. Druids will be allowed to participate.

Algae needs to be planted at the water area's endpoint to maintain the physical condition and hemoglobin index of the beasts.

trails.title: The Sacred Flame of Legend
trails.description: Among the many stories my grandmother shared with me, I'll never forget the one she told me about fire.

content.text: What are you doing? Why did you pick up that cold, opaque, opalescent glass wine bottle from the ground—at this most critical moment?
The scream outside the parking lot, the friction between the brake pads and the wheel drums, or the story unfolding like Giallo films. Obviously, none of them are as impressive as this bottle.
I can tell that you got good taste. You know it's not easy to get this stuff these days.
But, why are you staring at the bottom and licking your lips? Tell me, you are not going to take a sip, are you?
This is not a wise choice. You can't see the color of the liquid inside the glass. Maybe it's not the ice wine, or beer, or any homemade alcohol.
It's probably—very likely—just a critter's snot. Even so, do you still wanna give it a try?
Come off it. I'll take a shot.

branch.text: Every Carbuncle you've ever met will appreciate your courage.
Now, some cold liquid runs through your throat. It trickles slowly, most likely because it's thick. But the taste is much smoother than you think.
Then, a faint scent of absinthe greeted your nostril, and maltose, and lemon thyme, and coconut sugar. It's as delicious as a present from the arcanist from New Zealand.
And at the same time, your heart swells, and you feel a scorching energy fill your windpipe.
Your vision begins to blur. You kinda see the rough letter on the bottom: The Walden Potion Bar.
What the F**k is this?
It's anything but alcohol! "Alcohol" is a taboo. But it will empower you to face the next damn reality.
Who are you?
Me? Ha, I am no one.
But I can also be anyone—a drunken, slovenly old man, a cleaner in a run-down hotel, a fund manager greedy for more, or a cute spinning crystal skull.
Now I'm a drunkard with good taste, just like you.
And the day when we formally meet each other is coming soon.
Now, lift your big ass and continue your wonderful journey. I will appear at any time, any moment, no matter you expect or not.

content.text: I really shouldn't click this bottle.

branch.text: Right. It only took one moment for you to decide to click, while you had to stand so much nonsense for no reason.
My apologies if the story didn't unfold as you expected. But luckily, you still have your sanity that you are always proud of.
Come here. Let's put down the bottle. Before Sonetto and that floating APPLe notice your unusual behavior, you still have a chance to restore your image.
After me, say "Hi" to them. Pretend you've never been tempted by the bottle.
"Hi."
Oh. Hi! How are you doing?
Hahahahaha. Excellent. Now we all know how effective the training of the Foundation is. Good news: everyone likes good kids.
It's so nice talking to you. You're better than your ... Oops, I should stop here.
Who the hell are you?
Me? Ha, I am no one.
But I can also be anyone—a drunken, slovenly old man, a cleaner in a run-down hotel, a fund manager greedy for more, or a cute spinning crystal skull.
Now I am a nice and friendly adventurer, just like you.
Don't worry. The day when we formally meet each other is coming soon.
Now, lift your big ass and continue your wonderful journey. I will appear at any time, any moment, no matter you expect or not.
Are you sure they can hear it?

content.text: I really wanna find out what you're composed of! I'll chew and swallow all the gene analysis down to my stomach, so I can figure out ... how did you keep your sanity!
No arcanist is ever as rational and restrained as you. They should, they should ... If there is really one in the world, that should be ...
And I know so much about you. Too much about you! Even I cannot deny what you are. I can't!

branch.text: Me? Ha, I am no one.
But I can also be anyone—a drunken, slovenly old man, a cleaner in a run-down hotel, a fund manager greedy for more, or a cute spinning crystal skull.
But now I'm only a rubber asshole whose mischief just failed. A desperate loser. My wrath can't even burn a weed in the Pacific Ocean.
I'm looking forward to the day we formally meet each other. Only then …
Now, lift your big ass and continue your wonderful journey. I will appear at any time, any moment, no matter you expect or not!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Spathodea! Spathodea! Where, where did she go?!
It was like a long slumber, or a view of the garden behind the wall.
A new voice is heard coming alongside a gust of cold wind, blowing away the thick steam.
But now, I finally get to see the sun again. The world out there has completely changed.
The person made of fire opens her eyes. They are also filled with flame.
But you remain the same, Flammy, my dear friend.
You found me, and put an end to the long, dark dream. You set me on fire again, bringing me back to what a flame should be like.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Welcome to the end of the 20th century, Ulu.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: For you, this is an interesting era with many many new things. Well, I think we can learn them together later, one by one!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: While for my dear brave friends ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Welcome to the Uluru Games, my dear brave friends!
The giant heavy gate opens with winds blowing out from inside.
The team members go through the gate one after another. Ezra, however, remains still like a statue.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: What are you waiting for?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: The conjuring of the entrance to the Uluru Stadium is sourced from a fantastic arcane ritual. Instead of a summon, it's closer to a sacrifice ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: The fire element also plays an important part in this sacrifice. In Spathodea's case, Ulu is her flame.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Will it have anything to do with the unique condition Ms. Spathodea has? Unlike other "reincarnators," she still has a clear memory of this life, despite her young age.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Or, it's because that two light spots of hers—the older self and the modern self—are not that different, so she's spared going through any drastic changes, and the reason behind it might be ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ezra!!!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: ...! Yes, I'm here!
Ezra blinks several times, like a frightened animal, slowly looking up from the notebook.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: What can I do for you, Ms. Spathodea?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I'm waiting for you.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ah, I see. Sorry, I was too involved in taking notes.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I will pack and return to Laplace as soon as possible. But before that ...
After looking around a few times, Ezra pats his chest.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I have to clean up the spores and the mess we made in the battle first; otherwise, they may change the environment here.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Oh, c'mon, you weirdo!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You're leaving now, after all our effort? I can never understand you!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Aren't you waiting for me to leave?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Of course not! I'm waiting for you to join us. We'll go into the Stadium together!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Come to think about what I have suffered: coma, hallucination, confusion, thirst, misconception that I was almighty, and then, as you can see, I fell into a coma again after my sudden disappearance.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I think you're right. I do need a doctor by my side!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But mankind cannot enter the Stadium. We all know thaaaaaat ...!
An arm suddenly yanks Ezra into the gate.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ugh blah blah blah! Please, the Stadium has never shown itself to any humans before!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: When life gives you cake, just dig right in!
After the girl hops through it, the magnificent gate closes with a mighty snap.
Uluru Stadium

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Strewth! This is the Uluru Stadium?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's even more splendid than I thought, and ... more comfortable and pleasing.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Comfortable and pleasing?

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I don't feel the same way as you do.
Ezra takes a few steps ahead and matches them with deep breaths.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But not in the sense that this place doesn't look beautiful to me, on the contrary, it's stunning, but physically I don't feel anything special.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Maybe because you're a human. Hey, wait!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Mmm! Not so fast, be careful! Ms. Desert Flannel, you will fall!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I won't, I won't!
Desert Flannel stretches herself and suddenly steps firmly on the ground, running like an arrow toward Spathodea, who has already reached the other end of the field.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I'm feeling as light as the wind and even more energetic than when I finished a big meal of steak and cakes!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: I may fall anytime anywhere, but not now, not here!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: This is exactly what arcanists should feel.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ms. Ulu! Ah, pardon me. May I call you that?

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Go ahead if you want, child.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: But of course, I would appreciate it if you call me Madam, since I'm a few hundred years older than all of you. Besides, I am the most sacred flame of the Games ... Hmm?!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hah! I won! Been a long time since I had so much fun running!
Despite interrupting the conversation, Spathodea seems unfazed and keeps asking questions endlessly.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ulu! Is that a lawn? We didn't have anything like that before! And those benches!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Things change, Flammy.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: In the past hundreds of years when you were absent, countless changes happened to the Uluru Games.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: New lawns and benches had somehow appeared in the Stadium, but none of these changes was made by arcanists.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Those actually made by arcanists were new events, new rules, and new management. These are the changes that really made the Uluru Games different.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I see. No wonder I've never seen Ice Racewalking in my memories! Let me see, so there was no Stone Throw Divination or New Tridecathlon either ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Ice Racewalking is not a traditional sport in Australia. It originated from Northern Europe and became popular in cold countries.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: That's right. Ice Racewalking was introduced to the Games in 1926.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: If my memory serves me well, it was introduced by the St. Pavlov Foundation. On one hand, they hoped to show the internationality and inclusiveness of the Games; on the other ...

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: On the other?

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Well ... it took the place of Fire Racewalking.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: I see, I read it somewhere before. At the beginning of the 20th century, after St. Pavlov Foundation took over the Uluru Games, some challenging and relatively dangerous sports were canceled.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: This was also the turning point of the Uluru Games. From then on, the Games declined in popularity, and fewer and fewer athletes came each year.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Humph, these people ... No, these idiots! They know nothing about the essence of arcanists' sporting event!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Where on earth can you find an arcanist who would burn their own legs in Fire Racewalking?! Everyone knows you'll be fine as long as you believe the fire is harmless!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: But, in point of fact, fire is dangerous.
Ezra replies in a whisper and looks up, checking the roof from left to right.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: But think about it. It's unbelievable! Given your short fuse, I can't believe you just let them cancel your favorite event, Ulu.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Short ... fuse?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Yeah, you heard it right! She's got the hottest temper! Burns like herself!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Ahem! AHEM!!!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Things change, Flammy! I ... have already spent over a thousand years in this world. I'm no longer the young, hotheaded flame of your age!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Even your grandmother should call me Grandma now!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Grandma? So they can just take away your favorite event just because you're old now? I don't understand!
Walking a few steps away, Spathodea clenches her fists in anger.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Anyway, Flammy is back! It's time arcanists took back the Uluru Games from the Foundation! Let's design a new list of events that fit real arcanists!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: We'll start from Fire Racewalking. There are woods here. Ulu can start some bonfires with them ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Will the Foundation agree to this? They seem difficult to deal with.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: It's hard to take it over from the Foundation, but if we have all the security-related facilities prepared, and apply to host the event through Laplace Scientific Computing Center ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Considering Spathodea's identity, we do stand a chance.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But the paperwork we are going to deal with ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Oh, c'mon! COME ON! You are not supposed to talk about paperwork in the sacred Uluru Stadium!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Instead of a bunch of weak office workers who would pant from climbing a few stairs, what I need is some real athletes who can help me complete the Fire Racewalking!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I don't mind whether they are cute or weird, I only need them to be energetic! This is the only thing we ask of athletes in this sport ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Great idea. But the only inconvenience is that we are in the middle of the desert, a place where only flies visit.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: And as I checked my contact list, I saw only ... client, client, and client ... the ordinary ones and the ones I once stood up. Where are we going to find the athletes?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Well, I happen to know many arcanists who meet your need.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And they happen to be here right now.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: What? How come I can't see them anywhere?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hmm? Why are you opening the suitcase? Are you gonna organize your stuff here?
Open the suitcase, place it on the ground, and knock on the edge. A knocking sound echoes in the black space.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Anyone care to have some fresh air?
The other three standing around the suitcase look more puzzled. Spathodea tentatively opens her mouth but shuts it once again.
Soon a clear clip-clop comes from the bottomless suitcase.

items.speaker: Darley Clatter
items.text: *neigh*
The first thing they see is a silky, shining horse with a mane fluttering in the wind.

items.speaker: Darley Clatter
items.text: The fresh smell of grass with smoked fragrance! There is no doubt that it tastes better than gilded carrots!

items.speaker: Darley Clatter
items.text: And, look at this army of royal guards!

items.speaker: Darley Clatter
items.text: They must be here to greet the Great Darley Clatter!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Royal guards? What is he saying? Aaah ... no kidding, is that giant creature covered with spikes his "Royal Guard"?

items.speaker: Thorny Lizard
items.text: *roaring*
A deep, angry roar comes from the depths of the Stadium.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: That's the thorny devils, the enormous creatures born in the burning sand of the Stadium. They used to be mounts for the players, but looks like they have forgotten their master after all these years of slumber.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Enough talk. Let's put them back to dust and ashes.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Yes! Another great victory! And I dedicate this win to Ms. Spathodea!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: And to Ms. Desert Flannel!
Surrounded by the fiery atmosphere, the girls raise an invisible glass to each other.
Desert Flannel grabs Spathodea's wrist and lifts it up like a referee, calling out to the suitcase, out of which more arcanists pour out.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Now, people ... those of you who are not afraid of fire and wish to walk among the flames, please register here!
